Oelo vs DIY Permanent Lights: Professional Install Compared

Published July 1, 2026 | Reviewed October 29, 2026 | By CleanGutters Lighting

Permanent LED roofline lighting has grown popular across South Jersey, and homeowners are asking the practical question: can I save money by installing permanent lights myself?

There is no single right answer. It depends on your roofline, your comfort working on a ladder, how power reaches the roofline, and how much the written warranty and local service support matter to you. Here is an honest comparison of a DIY install and a professional Oelo installation.

What Is Oelo Permanent Lighting?

Oelo, LLC makes what it calls a permanent structural lighting system: LED lighting mounted along a home's roofline that stays up year-round and runs from a controller. You can switch colors for holidays, everyday accent lighting or special events without hanging lights every season. See our permanent outdoor lighting service for how this looks on South Jersey homes.

Oelo rates its lights for 100,000 hours. That is a rating, not a promise of how many years a particular system will last. Actual life depends on daily use, weather and the quality of the installation.

What Oelo's Warranty Actually Says

Oelo's published warranty, as reviewed on October 29, 2026:

  • Who is covered: the original property owner (not the installer), plus one later owner if the warranty is transferred within 60 days of a home sale.
  • How long: for systems installed on or after January 1, 2024, 7 years for installs by Oelo Authorized, Preferred and Platinum Dealers, and 5 years for contractor and customer DIY installs. Systems installed before that date carry 5 years.
  • First year: full coverage. Oelo may repair or replace products it determines are defective, including the labor directly required. Related work such as soffit, metalwork or flashing is not covered.
  • After the first year: component-only coverage for the rest of the term. Parts are covered for defects such as a failed LED, a controller failure or a clouded or yellowed lens, but labor is not included.
  • Claims: must be made within 30 days of finding the problem. Oelo decides whether a product is defective and how to compensate.
Correction: An earlier version of this article said self-installed Oelo systems have no manufacturer warranty. That was wrong. Oelo's published warranty includes a 5-year term for customer DIY installs. We cannot promise how a claim on any particular job will be decided; that depends on Oelo's written terms and its own review.

Where DIY Installs Commonly Go Wrong

  • Fit and measurements — Rooflines, fascia angles and soffit depths vary. Track or channel that is not measured and cut for the home can leave gaps, uneven runs and corners that look aftermarket.
  • Even brightness on long runs — Long runs of LEDs need power planned along the way. Without that planning, brightness or color can look uneven toward the end of a run.
  • Power and electrical work — Permanent exterior lighting needs a suitable power source. Whether your home needs a new outlet or circuit depends on the home. New electrical work must be handled by an appropriately qualified professional, and permit requirements depend on your town.
  • Water and sealing — Any fastener or wire that passes through fascia or soffit needs to be sealed so water does not reach the wood behind it.
  • Ladder safety — Roofline work means hours on a ladder. Read our ladder safety guide before you start.

What a Professional Install Should Include

Whoever you hire, the written estimate should cover:

1. Measurement and Layout

A measurement of your roofline, fascia and soffit, and a layout showing where runs, corners, the power supply and the controller will go.

2. Clean, Sealed Mounting

Track or channel fastened neatly along the roofline, with corners finished cleanly and every penetration sealed against South Jersey's nor'easters and summer storms.

3. Electrical Work, Clearly Assigned

If your home needs a new outlet or circuit, the estimate should say who will do that work. It must be handled by an appropriately qualified professional.

4. App Setup and Color Programming

Setup of the app, seasonal presets (red and green for Christmas, orange for Halloween, patriotic themes) and a walkthrough so you can create your own scenes.

5. Written Warranty and Service Support

The manufacturer's warranty in writing, the installer's own workmanship terms in writing, and a clear answer on who comes back if a light fails and whether labor is charged after the first year.

South Jersey Homes Have Unique Challenges

Our service area from Cherry Hill to Cape May includes homes built across several decades, with different fascia materials, soffit configurations and electrical setups. Things to plan for:

  • Older homes in Haddonfield and Collingswood can have narrow or older fascia boards that need careful mounting
  • Colonials and Capes in Medford and Marlton often have roofline angles that need precise corners
  • Shore homes in Ocean City and Brigantine face wind-driven rain, so sealing matters
  • New construction in Mullica Hill and Gibbsboro may need coordination with the builder's electrical plan

The Bottom Line for South Jersey Homeowners

A careful DIYer can install permanent lighting, and Oelo's warranty does cover customer DIY installs, though for a shorter term than eligible dealer installs. A professional install makes sense if you want the layout, ladder work, app setup and service handled for you, with the scope and warranty in writing.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I install Oelo lights myself and still have a warranty?

Yes. Oelo's published warranty lists a 5-year term for customer DIY installs, compared with 7 years for installs by Oelo Authorized, Preferred and Platinum Dealers on or after January 1, 2024. In both cases the first year is full coverage and later years are parts only. Check Oelo's current written terms before you buy.

Do I need an electrician?

It depends on the home. If you need a new outlet or circuit, that work must be handled by an appropriately qualified professional, and permit requirements depend on your town.

How long does professional installation take?

It depends on roofline length, layout and power access. Your installer should give you a schedule with the written estimate.

What if I already installed a DIY kit and it isn't working right?

Call us and we can take a look. If water is getting in around the fasteners, it's worth catching early, before it damages the fascia or soffit.
